_comment: THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION FOR THE S2 CUTOVER, IN ONE FILE.
The rehearsal script reads this; Abdullah's server tests pin the same file.
One source of truth, so the command and the rehearsal cannot drift apart.
`flips` lists the legacy feature ids whose `pivot.is_available` is LICENSED
to change from 1 to 0 in GET /api/mobile/masjids/{id}/features after the
cutover. An empty list means the payload must be wholly identical.
`decision` records WHERE each expectation comes from: `owner` means a person
chose it and it may be revisited; `rule` means it falls out of the literal
id-to-key mapping and changing it would mean changing the mapping.
`expect_shape_change` releases the row-set assertion for the ONE org whose
row set is meant to change. Nothing else is released.
HOW IT IS ENFORCED (compare_features.py): the licensed flips are patched back
out of the AFTER document, and the two documents must then be WHOLLY EQUAL.
Every unlicensed change therefore surfaces by construction, rather than only
the changes a reviewer happened to think of. Proven by audit-criterion.py,
which mutates a real capture seventeen ways and asserts each one is caught.
id -> key: 1 quran, 2 hadith, 3 adhkar, 4 qibla, 5 tasbih, 6 donation_link,
7 about_us, 8 gallery, 9 services, 10 announcements, 11 contact_requests.
KNOWN WEAKNESS, stated rather than left to inference: the org marked
`expect_shape_change` has no before-image, so it is checked for its row set,
integer-ness and icons only — names, keys and timestamps on its new rows are
NOT verified. Binding its eleven resolved values when
config/app_feature_cutover.php lands is what closes that gap.
`decision_taken_twice` marks an entry the owner approved, then approved AGAIN after
the consequence was re-described correctly. An approval obtained against a wrong
description is not an approval; these three were re-put and held.
A NOTE ON BUNDLES vs DEFAULTS, because the two are easy to conflate: `services` is
in ALL THREE vertical bundles in config/verticals.php, so it is not a masjid-only
module. What governs the school-side flips is the CAPABILITY default in
config/capabilities.php - `services` and `donation_link` both default to
masjid true / school false / community false. A bundle says what a tenant is seeded
with; a default says what a switch reads when nobody has set it. Different things.

1.name: Burlington Masjid
1.why: literal mapping; every row already agrees. Has Stripe Connect live and 10 active funds.

13.name: Muslim Education Center
13.why: Qur'an (id 1) is pivot OFF while the masjid worship module defaults ON, so the cutover writes an explicit quran=false. The MEC app does not show Qur'an today and must not start. Whether MEC wants it is a product question for after S2 - one visible, reversible switch, not something to smuggle into a migration. Donate stays: MEC has a real donation link.

14.name: Al-Razi School
14.why: OWNER 2026-09-16: turn the Donate row off. Al-Razi has no Stripe account, no active funds and no donation link, so the row leads to 'No donation options are available right now.' Leading people to an empty state is worse than not offering it, and it is one switch back the day they have a link. REAFFIRMED 2026-09-16 against the CORRECTED description. The decision was first taken when id 6 was described as a menu row leaving the app. It is not: on iPhone `MainTabView.swift:39` gates a bottom TAB on this id, so turning it off removes a tab and the tab bar re-lays out around it on a shipped build with no release. Abdullah put that shape to the owner explicitly, with reversal and BISS-only both on the table, and the answer was 'Off for all three, as decided.' A reader finding this entry should know somebody knowingly removed a tab from a live iPhone app - a rule did not sweep it up. SERVICES (id 9) OFF - owner, 2026-09-16. Measured first: all four orgs (14, 16, 18, 19) have ZERO service rows on production, so this switches off a module with nothing behind it. Not a separate judgement: it follows the same principle as the Donate call the owner took the same day, and it resolves an inconsistency where 19 had Services turned off by decision while 14, 16 and 18 kept it on only because no resolution had been written. The deciding point: `services` and `donation_link` carry IDENTICAL capability defaults (masjid true, school false, community false), so switching both off at these orgs RESTORES the vertical default. It is not taking something away from a school - it is ending an inheritance the school was never meant to have.

17.name: ZZ QA Sandbox
17.why: The only org with zero pivot rows, on staging and production alike: it serves [] today and eleven rows after the cutover. It is therefore the one org whose ROW SET changes, which `flips` cannot express - an earlier version of this file said 'no change' and would have failed the rehearsal with a misleading 'row order changed'. Unlisted, no installed app, so no real-world victim. The eleven resolved values are not pinned here yet because config/app_feature_cutover.php does not exist; bind them when it does. Its destination row set is pinned in `expected_row_ids` so the shape-change release is not a blanket waiver: it must land on exactly these eleven ids in this order.

19.name: MAS Youth Charlotte
19.why: OWNER: Donate stays, Services goes. donation_link stays ON because MAS Youth has a real donation link (masyouthclt.com) - it is the one org of the four where the Donate row leads somewhere. Worship stays off, already true. 2026-09-16 the owner extended this Services decision to 14, 16 and 18, which were in the identical zero-services state, so the four now agree.

invariants_that_hold_for_every_org: HTTP 200. Never 5xx, at any step of the fallback chain.
Row order and row names unchanged (Play vc13 positions tiles by index and routes by name).

pivot.is_available serialises as an INTEGER, never a boolean - Android's FeaturesResponse declares it Int, and Python's True == 1 means a bool passes naive equality while failing to decode on the device. Checked explicitly, not by comparison.
icon.original_url non-null on every row - a null force-unwraps in the Flutter drawer and blanks the grid (the 2026-08-28 incident).
The diff is taken only AFTER the cache flush is observed. A comparison made before flushFamily lands compares a cached pre-cutover payload with itself: it matches and proves nothing.
